prov.text: The provision for credit losses was $1.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to a provision for credit losses of $5.9 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026. The provision for credit losses for the quarter was driven by an increase in the ACL – Loans of $1.2 million, net charge-offs of $1.2 million, and a decrease in the ACL – Unfunded of $1.0 million. The provision for credit losses in the prior quarter was driven by an increase in the ACL – Loans of $1.8 million, net charge-offs of $2.7 million, and an increase in the ACL – Unfunded of $1.4 million. Net charge-offs for the quarterly periods that relate to legacy Consumer and Commercial and Industrial forward flow loans were $0.8 million and $1.7 million, respectively for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and June 30, 2026.

nonint.heading: Non-interest Expense
nonint.text:
The following table presents non-interest expense for three months ended September 30, 2026 and June 30, 2026 and for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 and the change between periods, by major component:

Total non-interest expense was $70.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $4.6 million, or 7.0%, compared with the three months ended June 30, 2026, primarily due to the combination of (i) an increase in incentive bonus compensation, (ii) legal and sub-servicer fees related to the Solar Servicing business, which are largely reimbursed by counterparties to the loans and recognized in other non-interest income and other corporate legal fees, and (iii) one additional month of expenses related to the ownership of the Company’s headquarters following the building acquisition in April 2026.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense
nonop.text:
Interest expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026, was $75.4 million compared to $65.9 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, an increase of $9.5 million, or 14.4%, was primarily related to an increase in Digital Banking deposits, an additional day in the quarter, and a one basis point increase in the cost of interest-bearing liabilities.

Interest expense for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was $205.5 million compared to $188.0 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $17.5 million, or 9.3%, was primarily related to an increase in average balances of $879.8 million in Digital Banking deposits and $526.1 million in third-party sweep deposits largely offset by a 35 basis point decrease in the average rate paid on interest-bearing deposits and a decrease in average balance of $121.2 million in brokered deposits.

pretax.text: • Pre provision net revenue - We calculate pre provision net revenue by adding provision for credit losses to income before income taxes.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
For the three months ended September 30, 2026, income tax expense and the effective tax rate were $8.5 million and 29.0%, respectively, compared to $9.2 million and 69.0%, respectively for the three months ended June 30, 2026. Income tax expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026 reflects the recognition of $2.7 million of deferred credit amortization that was offset by a purchase accounting adjustment of $2.7 million for previously recognized amortization, resulting in no net impact from the deferred credit in the quarter. The purchase accounting adjustment was related to the completion of the final tax return for the acquired entity. Income tax expense for the three months ended June 30, 2026, included (i) a $5.6 million write-down of deferred tax assets as of December 31, 2025, for stock compensation in connection with the initial public offering, which is due to tax rules that limit executive compensation deductions for public companies, and (ii) a $1.1 million benefit for amortization of the deferred credit.

The effective tax rate for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was 29.0%, compared to 69.0% for the three months ended June 30, 2026.

net.text: • Return on average tangible common equity - We calculate return on average tangible common equity by dividing adjusted net income for the period by average tangible common equity over the same period. Adjusted net income, used for the calculation of return on average tangible common equity, is calculated by adding back the tax effected amount of intangible asset amortization to net income.

ocf.heading: Net cash used in operating activities
ocf.text:
Cash used in operating activities of $44.8 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was primarily driven by originations of loans held-for-sale and the amortization of deferred loan fees and costs, offset by net income for the period, changes in deferred income taxes, and changes in interest receivable.

Cash used in operating activities of $61.0 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, was primarily driven by changes in other assets, originations of loans held-for-sale, the amortization of deferred loan fees and costs, and changes in interest receivable, offset by net income for the period.

sbc.text: Compensation and benefits expenses were $101.5 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $7.8 million, or 8.3%, compared to $93.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, primarily due to a $5.2 million increase in base compensation related to a full year of compensation paid to employees added in the Solar Servicing business acquisition and from expanding our Digital Banking, Asset Finance and Fund Finance teams, a $5.0 million increase in stock-based compensation, and $2.0 million from the personnel retention compensation program implemented in connection with our initial public offering. Those increases were partially offset by a $3.1 million decrease in the annual bonus accrual and $2.9 million from an increase in deferred compensation recognized related to higher loan originations during the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text:
The following table discloses the components of net interest income for three months ended September 30, 2026 and June 30, 2026 and for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025:

Net interest income for the three months ended September 30, 2026, was $72.0 million compared with $63.1 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, an increase of $8.8 million, or 13.9%, was primarily related to an increase in interest income of $18.3 million offset by an increase in interest expense of $9.5 million.

Net interest income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was $194.7 million compared with $196.0 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, a decrease of $1.3 million, or 0.7%, was primarily related to an increase in interest expense of $17.5 million marginally exceeding an increase in interest income of $16.2 million.

intro.text: Forbright, Inc., a Delaware corporation, is a bank holding company that along with its subsidiaries, is headquartered in Chevy Chase, Maryland. Forbright Bank, a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, is a Maryland state-chartered non-member bank, which serves the needs of individuals, small and medium sized businesses, and professional concerns. Nationwide, the Bank serves deposit and retail banking customers via its digital deposit platform and offers competitive financing and lending services, originating term loans, working capital facilities, warehouse lines of credit, and leases.

accounts.name: Property, plant and equipment
accounts.note: Depreciation and amortisation includes the amortisation of intangibles where the filing reports one line: the PP&E residual then carries the intangibles' share.

accounts.name: Goodwill and intangibles
accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.
